newsitem.title: UK: NYMEX sees Cusiana deliverability on crude in Q1.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX sees Cusiana deliverability on crude in Q1.

text.p: Colombia's Cusiana crude oil is expected to be deliverable against the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) crude contract in the first quarter of 1997, NYMEX Chairman Daniel Rappaport said on Tuesday.

The move to include the Latin American crude is part of the exchange's broad efforts to boost trading interest on the continent which eventually could include a link with the Sao Paulo futures exchange and an ethanol contract, he said.
NYMEX's crude advisory committee has already met a number of times on the Cusiana issue and it is expected to be on the agenda at its next meeting in November, he added.
Once it passes the committee and the board, then the Commodity Futures Trading Commission would have to give its approval.
"We're looking at the first quarter of 1997," Rappaport told a news conference during his visit to London Metal Exchange Week.
Crude has played an increasing role in U.S. oil markets in the last year, which traders said prompted this interest.

British Petroleum, operator of the huge Colombian oilfield on the Llanos Orientales or eastern plains, expects output there in 1996 to rise to 180,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 128,000 bpd in 1995, and to hit 500,000 bpd by the year 2000.
Rappaport said NYMEX hoped to offer its electronic trading system, dubbed ACCESS, in the Sao Paulo futures market, BM&F, some time after June 1998 when it can boost its technological capabilities.
"We have a geographical disadvantage to Asia and Europe and we think we have a geographic advantage both in proximity and time (zones) to Latin America," he said.
